To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the middle face patch is a face feature space that encodes the geometry of facial elements and that this geometry is defined relative to an entire, upright face.
cells in the middle temporal area are tuned to the magnitude of face parts and that tuning amplitude depends on the presence of the whole, upright face.
cells in the middle macaque face patch detect and differentiate faces by detecting and discriminating constellations of facial features and by tuning to the geometry of those features.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the principles of neural coding for face perception in the primate brain, and in particular, how face perception relates to other forms of object and pattern perception.
how the brain represents faces and the mechanisms that underlie face recognition.
the analysis of faces by the visual system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the middle face patch is a face space that is specialized for the detection and differentiation of whole, upright faces.
the middle face patch contains neurons with face-selective responses that are part based but also holistic in that they depend on the context of the face as a whole.
the middle face patch is a face feature space in which neurons encode axes of a holistic face space.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
face perception in primates is not based on an abstract face representation, but on the analysis of facial features.
middle face patch cells are tuned to the geometry and position of facial features in whole, upright faces and that this information is used to differentiate faces.
face-selective cells are not only selective for faces, they are tuned to the geometry and spatial arrangement of face features.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the face space in the middle face region of the macaque temporal cortex is specialized for whole, frontal, upright faces.
face perception in primates is supported by a distributed system of face-selective neurons that encode the geometry of facial parts.
the middle face patch is a part-based face space that is tuned to the geometry and position of face features.
